wu: Students stand in a circle and play 'Two Truths and a Lie' about their recent reading habits, e.g., 'I read a news article yesterday,' 'I love scanning for numbers,' 'I never skim headings.'
wuAlt: Students share one reading strategy they used this week with a partner.
Students quickly list 3 things they remember about PET reading parts from last class.
pres: Display a PET reading part 1 text on the board. Model skimming (reading headings in 30 sec), scanning (finding dates in 20 sec), and detail reading (answering Q3 in 45 sec). Check understanding by asking: 'Which strategy finds specific info?'
presAlt: Hand out a short article with questions; model marking the text for each strategy.
Use a think-aloud: 'I see the title, so I'll skim first...'
prac: Students work in pairs to time each other on a PET reading part 1 text (3 min). They swap papers and use a checklist to mark which strategy their partner used. Teacher circulates to monitor timing.
pracAlt: Students race to scan for answers in different texts, then compare with the answer key.
Groups complete a 'strategy match' worksheet linking questions to skimming/scanning/detail.
ls: Students listen to a short audio recording of someone discussing their reading strategies (2 min). They tick the strategies mentioned (skimming, scanning, etc.) and discuss in pairs if they agree.
re: Students play 'Strategy Charades'—one student acts out skimming (fast hand movements over text) or scanning (pointing quickly), others guess the term.
prod: In trios, students take turns explaining how they would solve a PET reading part 2 text (matching headings to paragraphs). They justify their choices using 'I skimmed the headings first...' or 'I scanned for keywords...'
rw: Students complete a timed PET reading part 3 text (multiple-choice) individually (7 min). They then swap papers and discuss answers in pairs, explaining their reasoning using 'I chose B because...'
st: Read a short story about a student who improved their PET score using better strategies. End with: 'Today we practiced timed PET reading strategies. Thank you for your hard work!'
g: Students race to find the main idea of a text in 30 sec.
Students scan for numbers/words and call them out.
Students find and underline answers to detail questions.
Groups sort questions into skimming/scanning/detail piles.
Teams answer questions about PET reading parts.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 2 tips for timed reading success.
Support learners: Use a highlighter to mark key words before answering.
hw: Complete a timed PET reading part 1 at home and record your score.
Write 3 sentences about which strategy you found easiest/hardest.
Review the PET reading strategies in your folder.
tip: Encourage students to reflect on their timing—many spend too long on one part. A stopwatch is your best tool for building exam pace.
